sections.instruction: Write a suitable sentence using the PRESENT PERFECT TENSE: (Example: Ann’s hair was dirty. Now it’s clean. (wash) → Ann has washed her hair.)

questions.prompt: Tom was 80 kg. Now he’s 70. (lose weight)
questions.explanation: present perfect: past action with a result now

questions.prompt: Bill played football yesterday. Now he can’t walk; his leg is in plaster. (break)
My sister is looking for her pen. (lose)
acceptedAnswers: My sister has lost her pen.

questions.prompt: Mary is on holiday in France. (go)
acceptedAnswers: Mary has gone on holiday to France.
She has gone on holiday to France.
She's gone on holiday to France.
questions.explanation: has gone = went and is still there

questions.prompt: Mr. Hill was in Canada last week. He’s back in London now. (be)

questions.prompt: Look! Mrs. Smith has got a lot of packages. (buy)

questions.prompt: I can’t eat anything now. (eat too much)

sections.instruction: Rewrite the sentences using the SIMPLE PAST or the PRESENT PERFECT TENSE: (Example: I haven’t seen her for a long time. → It’s ages since I saw her.)

questions.prompt: I last met George two weeks ago. → I haven’t
acceptedAnswers: I haven't met George for two weeks.
I haven't seen George for two weeks.
I haven't met him for two weeks.

questions.prompt: They have been here for three months. → They arrived
acceptedAnswers: They arrived here three months ago.
questions.explanation: for (up to now) → simple past + ago

questions.prompt: We started living in Istanbul 12 years ago. → We have
acceptedAnswers: We have lived in Istanbul for 12 years.
We've lived in Istanbul for 12 years.
We have been living in Istanbul for 12 years.
We've been living in Istanbul for 12 years.
We have lived in Istanbul for twelve years.
We've lived in Istanbul for twelve years.
We have been living in Istanbul for twelve years.
We've been living in Istanbul for twelve years.

questions.prompt: I last saw my girlfriend five days ago. → I haven’t
acceptedAnswers: I haven't seen my girlfriend for five days.
I haven't seen her for five days.

questions.prompt: Is this the first time you have tasted a kiwi? → Use (not) + you, and end with “one before?”
acceptedAnswers: Have you not tasted one before?
Haven't you ever tasted one before?

questions.prompt: I last smoked a cigarette ten years ago. → I haven’t
acceptedAnswers: I haven't smoked a cigarette for ten years.
I haven't smoked for ten years.

questions.prompt: I last drank wine two weeks ago. → Start with “It’s two weeks” and end with “wine”.
acceptedAnswers: It's two weeks since I last drank wine.
It's two weeks since I drank wine.
It's been two weeks since I last drank wine.

questions.prompt: I have lived in Istanbul since January. → I (come)
acceptedAnswers: I came to Istanbul in January.

questions.prompt: They moved to Ankara two years ago. → Start with “They” and end with “two years”.
acceptedAnswers: They have lived in Ankara for two years.
They've lived in Ankara for two years.
They have been living in Ankara for two years.
They've been living in Ankara for two years.
They have been in Ankara for two years.
They've been in Ankara for two years.

questions.prompt: She hasn’t been to Rome before. → This is the first time
acceptedAnswers: This is the first time she has been to Rome.
This is the first time she's been to Rome.
This is the first time she has ever been to Rome.
This is the first time she's ever been to Rome.
